articles.title: The actions inbox
articles.summary: Every change the assistant proposes waits here until you approve or reject it.

blocks.text: The actions inbox lists proposals made by the assistant and by automated helpers. Each shows what it would change and why.
Deciding
For each proposal you can **approve**, **reject**, or, after approving, **undo** where the change can be reversed. Nothing happens until you approve.
What it cannot do
Some changes cannot be undone, such as a message that has already been sent. Those are labelled before you approve.

articles.title: The assistant
articles.summary: Ask questions about your own data; anything that changes something is proposed first.

blocks.text: The assistant answers questions using the data in the workspace you are in: your pipeline, contacts, calls and documents.
Reading and proposing

Reading is immediate. When an answer would **change** something, such as moving an investor to a new stage or creating a follow-up task, the assistant does not do it. It adds a proposal to the [actions inbox](/dashboard/help/actions-inbox), where you approve or reject it.
Good questions

items: Which investors have not replied in two weeks?
Summarise my last call with this investor.
What is missing from my data room?

blocks.text: What it cannot do

The assistant can be wrong. Check names, numbers and dates before you rely on them. It cannot send email or messages by itself and it does not see other workspaces. Use of it counts against your workspace's monthly allowance on the **Usage** page.

articles.title: Command palette and shortcuts
articles.summary: Jump to any page from the keyboard.

blocks.text: Press **Ctrl K** (Windows, Linux) or **Cmd K** (Mac) anywhere in the app to open the command palette. Type part of a page name and press Enter.
What it cannot do
It lists pages your role and plan can open. A page that is missing from it is not available to your workspace; see [Workspaces, roles and switching](/dashboard/help/workspaces-and-roles).

articles.title: Find investors and what the score means
articles.summary: How matching ranks investors for your round, and how to read the tiers.

blocks.text: Find investors ranks investors against your company profile. Each result has a score from 0 to 100, built from six factors: investor type, cheque size, sector, geography, thesis and whether a contact is known.
Tiers
Using it
Open a result to see why it ranked where it did, then save it to your [pipeline](/dashboard/help/pipeline).
What it cannot do

A score is a ranking aid, not a prediction that an investor will invest. Where a fact is unknown the score says so rather than guessing. Complete your company profile first, because the ranking can only be as good as what it knows about you.

articles.title: LinkedIn outreach (assisted sending)
articles.summary: Messages are written in Anker and sent by you from your own LinkedIn.

blocks.text: LinkedIn outreach is **assisted**: Anker prepares the message and the browser extension shows it in a panel, but you send it yourself.
What it cannot do
It does not send from your account on its own. Sending is limited by LinkedIn's own rules, which Anker does not control.

articles.title: Outreach: drafts, approval and limits
articles.summary: How messages to investors are drafted, approved and sent.

blocks.text: Outreach drafts messages for investors in your pipeline. You review each draft before anything is sent.
The flow

items: Review the drafts and edit them.
Approve. Only approved messages are sent.

blocks.text: Limits
Your plan sets a daily sending limit. When you reach it, further messages wait for the next day.
What it cannot do
Whether a message reaches an inbox, and whether anyone replies, is outside Anker's control.

articles.title: Your fundraising pipeline
articles.summary: Track each investor from first contact to a decision.

blocks.text: The pipeline shows every investor you are talking to, grouped by stage. Move an investor between stages as the conversation progresses.
Stages

Stages run in order from the first, queued, to a final decision. The underlying order is: queued, identified, researched, contacted, responded, meeting, diligence, soft_circle, term_sheet, committed, wired, passed, declined, lost. Your workspace may show friendlier names for the same steps.
What it cannot do
Moving a card does not email anyone. If the assistant suggests a stage change, it appears in the [actions inbox](/dashboard/help/actions-inbox) for you to approve.

articles.title: Privacy in plain words
articles.summary: Who can see what in your workspace.

blocks.text: Your workspace's records are visible to the people you invite to it. They are kept apart from every other workspace.
Platform operators
The people who run Anker can see how the platform is used, such as counts and errors. They are firewalled from the private records of a workspace.
The assistant
The assistant reads your workspace data to answer you. Your records are not shared with other workspaces.
What it cannot do
This page is a summary, not a contract. Your agreement and privacy policy are the binding terms.

articles.title: Welcome to Anker
articles.summary: What Anker is, how it is organised, and where to start.

blocks.text: Anker is a workspace for raising and managing capital. What you see depends on your role: founders get fundraising tools, funds get deal and investor tools, and limited partners get a read-only view of their own holdings.
How the menu is organised

The menu groups pages by the work you do, not by feature name. Founders see areas such as Fundraising, Relationships, Outreach, Company, Documents and Assistant. Funds see Deals, Portfolio, Investors, Fund operations, Reporting and Assistant. Limited partners see Assistant, Capital activity and Documents.
Where to start

items: Open the **Assistant** and ask a question about your own data.
Use the **command palette** (Ctrl K, or Cmd K on a Mac) to jump to any page by name.
Read [Workspaces, roles and switching](/dashboard/help/workspaces-and-roles) so you know whose data you are looking at.

blocks.text: What it cannot do
Anker does not move money, and it does not send messages or change records without you approving them. Some pages only appear when your workspace's plan includes them.

articles.title: Workspaces, roles and switching
articles.summary: A workspace holds one organisation's data; your role decides what you see in it.

blocks.text: A **workspace** is one organisation's space: its profile, contacts, documents and history. Everything you create belongs to the workspace, not to you personally, so a colleague you invite sees the same records.
Roles

Your role in a workspace sets the menu you see. A person can belong to more than one workspace and switch between them. When you switch, the menu, the assistant and every number on screen change to that workspace.
Inviting people
Open **Settings** to invite a colleague. The number of seats is set by your workspace's plan.
What it cannot do
Switching workspace does not copy data between them. A workspace owner's private records are not visible to the platform's operators.
